## Option A (Tier P) — vendor eval

If you have an Infoblox or BlueCat evaluation, use it: create three DNS
views (internal / cloud-internal / external), enable DNSSEC on one zone,
and run the vendor's IPAM export — then skip to
[Bind the evidence](#bind-the-evidence). The
[vendor catalog](../vendor-training-catalog.html#networking-ddi) lists both
vendors' training portals, which include lab guides for their own products.

## Option B (Tier F) — containerized split-horizon lab

No license needed: two BIND views + Kea DHCP in containers approximate the
Book 01 split-horizon exercise.

```bash
mkdir -p ddi-lab/{internal,external} && cd ddi-lab

# internal view zone: returns a private address
cat > internal/db.app.example.test <<'EOF'
$TTL 300
@ IN SOA ns1.example.test. admin.example.test. (1 3600 900 604800 300)
@ IN NS  ns1.example.test.
app IN A 10.20.0.15
EOF

# external view zone: same name does NOT exist (NXDOMAIN goal),
# only public names are present
cat > external/db.example.test <<'EOF'
$TTL 300
@ IN SOA ns1.example.test. admin.example.test. (1 3600 900 604800 300)
@ IN NS  ns1.example.test.
www IN A 203.0.113.10
EOF
```

`named.conf` with two views keyed by client subnet (the lab's stand-in for
Book 01's internal vs. external resolvers):

```text
view "internal" {
  match-clients { 127.0.0.0/8; 10.0.0.0/8; };   # loopback = internal (exec into container); docker bridge source falls to external
  zone "app.example.test" { type primary; file "/etc/bind/internal/db.app.example.test"; };
};
view "external" {
  match-clients { any; };
  zone "example.test" { type primary; file "/etc/bind/external/db.example.test"; };
};
```

Run it and verify the split:

```bash
docker run -d --name ddi-bind -v "$PWD:/etc/bind" -p 5353:53/udp internetsystemsconsortium/bind9:9.18

# internal client (simulate with source routing or exec into the container):
docker exec ddi-bind dig @127.0.0.1 app.app.example.test A +short   # → 10.20.0.15
# external client:
dig @127.0.0.1 -p 5353 app.app.example.test A                      # → NXDOMAIN  ✅ Book 01's requirement
```

## Exercise — the M365 endpoint poll pipeline

Book 01's automation lab, runnable anywhere with Python:

```python
# m365_endpoints_diff.py — poll the Microsoft 365 IP & URL web service,
# diff versions, and emit the allow/block artifacts Book 01 automates.
import json, urllib.request, uuid, pathlib

CLIENT = uuid.uuid4()
SERVICE = "endpoints.office.com"  # M365 IP & URL web service host
url = "https://" + SERVICE + "/endpoints/worldwide?clientrequestid=" + str(CLIENT)
data = json.load(urllib.request.urlopen(url))

prev = pathlib.Path("m365-endpoints.json")
old = json.loads(prev.read_text()) if prev.exists() else []
old_urls = {u for e in old for u in e.get("urls", [])}
new_urls = {u for e in data for u in e.get("urls", [])}

print("ADD  →", sorted(new_urls - old_urls)[:10])
print("DROP →", sorted(old_urls - new_urls)[:10])
prev.write_text(json.dumps(data, indent=1))
# In production these diffs drive RPZ allow/block, NSG, and split-tunnel updates.
```

## Bind the evidence {#bind-the-evidence}

Produce the CM-8-shaped inventory artifact (from the vendor export in
Option A, or hand-built from the lab's address plan in Option B):

```json
{
  "generated_at": "<timestamp>",
  "source": "ddi-lab",
  "networks": [
    {"cidr": "10.20.0.0/24", "view": "internal", "purpose": "app tier"},
    {"cidr": "203.0.113.0/24", "view": "external", "purpose": "public"}
  ],
  "records": [
    {"fqdn": "app.app.example.test", "ip": "10.20.0.15", "view": "internal"}
  ]
}
```

Reference it from a copy of the slot-02 mapping
([`slot-02-addressing-evidence.yaml`](https://github.com/WhalerMike/uiao/blob/main/src/uiao/adapters/fedramp_aan_catalog/mappings/slot-02-addressing-evidence.yaml))
and regenerate: `<engine> oscal ksi-ar --output exports/oscal/ksi-ar.json`.
Score yourself against the [slot 2 rubric](../assessment-rubrics.html#slot-2).

## Teardown

```bash
docker rm -f ddi-bind && rm -rf ddi-lab
```
